itemListElement.name: What Is a Discovery Call and How US Sales Teams Run One Well in 2026

mainEntity.name: What is the main purpose of a discovery call?

acceptedAnswer.text: To understand the prospect's problem, priorities, decision process and timeline, and to decide together whether there is a fit worth pursuing. One number worth knowing: Gong found the average seller talks 60% of a call, while reps who won talked 57%, so the gap is smaller than most coaching suggests.

mainEntity.name: How long is a discovery call?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most run about 30 minutes. Salesforce advises under 60 minutes, 20 to 30 for a simple transactional sale, and up to an hour across several calls for a complex enterprise deal. Book 30 by default, and keep the last 5 minutes for agreeing the next step.

mainEntity.name: Is a discovery call an interview?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not exactly. Think two-way conversation. While the seller asks most of the questions, the buyer should also learn something useful and decide whether to continue, leaving with a clearer view of their own problem and options. Good calls feel useful to the buyer.

In sales, yes: they are part of the sales process. Coaches and consultants also usually offer free discovery calls of 15 to 30 minutes. In law, a first consultation may be free or paid depending on the firm, so check before booking.

mainEntity.name: What happens after a discovery call?

acceptedAnswer.text: After the call, the seller sends a recap and, if there is a fit, books the next step, often a demo with additional stakeholders or a proposal review. Send that recap the same day, using the prospect's own words for their goals, challenges and timeline.

mainEntity.name: What is another name for a discovery call?

acceptedAnswer.text: You may also hear it called a discovery meeting, a qualification call, a needs analysis call or, for consultants and coaches, a consultation call.
